ledger.claim: The fee is chargeable only if all four limbs of POL-NS-01 hold, and limb (c) requires a continuous dwell of at least the 300-second LARGE_VENUE minimum measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, not from the arrival marker. On the driver's own clean trace the longest continuous in-geofence run is 170 seconds (19:00:00 to 19:02:50), 130 seconds short of that minimum. The primary clause therefore does not make this wait sufficient, and the charge can stand only if the separate in-geofence intervals are added together at all.

The rider's complaint is exactly what the trace records: the driver was outside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius from 19:02:50 to 19:03:50, a 60-second absence during which he reached 179.8 m from the pin, and his own message at 19:02:30 announced that he had to circulate and would return to the same bay. A 170-second hold and a 160-second hold are not one continuous hold; the charge survives only if POL-NS-06(i) lets them be summed, and even then the accumulated 330 seconds clears the 300-second minimum by just 30 seconds (derived shortfall -30 s).

The trip record's wait_time_min of 6.2 minutes is not the measure POL-NS-01 limb (c) prescribes. It runs from the arrival marker and includes the 60 seconds during which the vehicle was away from the bay circulating, whereas the clause measures in-geofence dwell from the first qualifying fix. An elapsed six-minute figure taken from the trip record cannot supply the continuity that limb (c) requires and that the trace's 170-second longest run does not show.

The rider's own position and the rider's silence are not part of this arithmetic. POL-NS-06 directs the refund to be decided on the dwell computation 'whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages', so the rider's track and the absence of any rider message during the waiting window cannot be used to convert a short in-geofence hold into a chargeable fee.

POL-NS-07 makes driver compensation payable only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it. Because the continuous-dwell limb is not made out on the primary clause and the whole dispute is about whether the two holds may be added, the precondition for the SGD 3.20 compensation figure itemised in the fare breakdown is absent and no driver payment should issue.

The whole of the contested amount sits on the rider: the fare breakdown shows a single SGD 4.00 cancellation fee, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, with no booking or platform fee component to apportion. If the dwell requirement is not satisfied the cancellation-fee line falls away in full under POL-NS-06 and the return to the rider is the entire SGD 4.00.

The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 2026-09-07T19:00:20+08:00 for TRP-09107, which satisfies limb (a) of POL-NS-01: the baseline chargeable no-show requires a recorded arrival event and this record has one.

The GPS trace places the driver inside the 120 m arrival radius for this LARGE_VENUE pickup: 35 of his 40 fixes qualify, including an unbroken qualifying run of 170 seconds from 19:00:00 to 19:02:50. Limb (b) of POL-NS-01 is met and the POL-NS-02 proximity test is satisfied on admissible, in-radius fixes.

The two in-geofence intervals total 330 seconds of dwell, against a POL-NS-01 minimum of 300 seconds for LARGE_VENUE, and POL-NS-06(i) expressly permits separate in-geofence intervals within a single pickup attempt to be summed where the driver never travelled more than 300 m from the pin.

Summation under POL-NS-06(i) is available on this record because every condition is met: a traffic advisory of type CLOSURE (EV-ADVIS-09107-01) covers the pickup road with an active window of 18:50 to 19:30, which covers the waiting period, and the driver's furthest point between the two intervals was 179.76 m from the pin, comfortably inside the 300 m leash.

The rider's central argument - that the car left the bay and the separate waits must not count together - is answered on the face of the clause she invokes: POL-NS-06(i) permits summation precisely where an admissible advisory made holding position unlawfully impossible, and here the advisory is present and populated at weight 1.0 rather than MISSING, so the shortfall calculation runs on 330 accumulated seconds, not on the 170 second longest single run.

The trip was terminated by the driver at 19:06:30 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW and no boarding event is recorded, so limb (d) of POL-NS-01 is satisfied: the termination is by the driver, under a recognised reason code, at a time after the required dwell had elapsed.

The chat log corroborates the driver's account rather than contradicting it: at 19:02:30 he messaged that the kerb was temporarily closed and that he must circulate and would return to the same bay, and at 19:04:05 he reported he was back at the marked bay - conduct consistent with lawful circulation under POL-NS-06(i), not abandonment of the pickup.

The arrival marker is not a false marker within POL-NS-05: at 19:00:20 the driver was already inside the 120 m arrival radius, far short of the 300 m threshold that clause sets, and the dwell began at that same first qualifying fix, so no recomputation of the waiting clock is triggered.

The rider's own GPS track is affirmatively against her presence at the pickup: every rider fix sits 519.37 m from the pin, well outside the 150 m rider-presence radius for LARGE_VENUE, so the only rider-position evidence on the record is against her rather than excusing her under POL-NS-04(c).

No message in the chat log was sent by the rider - the three entries are one SYSTEM arrival notice and two DRIVER messages - so limb (a) of POL-NS-04 is not met and that rider-exonerating clause cannot apply on these facts.

The SGD 4.00 cancellation fee in the fare breakdown reconciles with the fee_schedule resolution rule: the GREATER of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00) is SGD 4.00, so there is no integrity defect under POL-NS-08(d) and nothing to disturb in the charged amount.

With POL-NS-01 satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, POL-NS-07 pays the driver 80 percent of the SGD 4.00 fee, being SGD 3.20, and the anti-farming check does not trip: no_show_terminations_30d is 1 (below the threshold of 4) and 1 divided by 120 completed trips in 30 days is 0.008 (below 0.08), so compensation is payable rather than withheld.

No POL-NS-09 escalation trigger is engaged: rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d are both 0, and rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, so this case is decidable on its merits and should resolve to the driver's monetary outcome rather than being held for review.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the SGD 4.00 no-show fee charged to the rider stands, and the driver is paid SGD 3.20 (80% of that fee). The case turns on whether the two stretches the car spent at the bay may be added together, and on this record they may.

Why the fee stands. POL-NS-01 requires four things, and all four hold. (a) The trip record records the driver's arrival at 19:00:20. (b) The GPS trace places him inside the 120 m arrival radius for this LARGE_VENUE pickup from 19:00:00, before that arrival marker; his closest fix was about 26 m from the pin and 35 of his 40 fixes qualify. (d) He terminated the trip at 19:06:30 under RIDER_NO_SHOW with no boarding event, after the required dwell had accrued.

The disputed limb (c) – the 300-second dwell. The rider is right about the raw trace: the driver held for 170 seconds (19:00:00–19:02:50), left for 60 seconds, and held again for 160 seconds (19:03:50–19:06:30), so the longest single continuous hold is 170 seconds, 130 seconds short of 300. But POL-NS-06(i) expressly permits separate in-geofence intervals within one pickup attempt to be summed where the driver never travelled more than 300 m from the pin and a qualifying traffic advisory made holding position unlawfully impossible. Both conditions are met. His furthest point while circulating was 179.8 m from the pin, inside the 300 m leash, and LTA advisory ADV-20260907-01 is a CLOSURE covering the pickup road with an active window of 18:50 to 19:30, which covers the whole waiting period. The effective dwell is therefore 330 seconds, clearing the 300-second minimum by 30 seconds. His in-app messages at 19:02:30 ('kerb temporarily closed; I must circulate and will return to the same bay') and 19:04:05 ('Back at the marked bay now') describe exactly that lawful circulation, not an abandonment of the pickup.

The rider's point that trip_record.wait_time_min of 6.2 minutes is not the clause's yardstick is accepted: limb (c) measures in-geofence dwell from the first qualifying fix, not elapsed time from the arrival tap. It changes nothing here, because the properly measured dwell still meets the minimum. The rider's own absence from the pin (her fixes sit about 519 m away, outside the 150 m rider radius) and her silence in the chat likewise do not move the fee: POL-NS-06 decides the refund on the dwell arithmetic whether or not the rider was present or responsive. POL-NS-04 cannot apply because no rider locating message was sent, and POL-NS-05 does not apply because the arrival marker was placed while the driver sat inside the radius and stationary, not beyond 300 m or in motion.

Driver compensation. With POL-NS-01 satisfied and nothing in POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, POL-NS-07 pays the driver 80% of SGD 4.00, being SGD 3.20. The anti-farming check does not trip: 1 no-show termination in 30 days is below 4, and 1 divided by 120 completed trips is 0.008, below 0.08. Compensation is therefore payable rather than withheld, and the rider's charge stands.

Confidence. Every artifact the ruling rests on – the GPS trace, trip record, chat log, fare breakdown and traffic advisory – carries weight 1.0 with no integrity defect under POL-NS-08 (no clock skew, no trace gap, the chat matches the trip record's message count, and the SGD 4.00 fee equals the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee), so nothing is discounted. No POL-NS-09 escalation trigger is engaged, and no clause directs a referral.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
